key_insight: An equivariant graph neural network can predict frequency-dependent complex dynamic polarizability tensors of organic molecules directly from molecular structure and spectra, closely matching TD-DFT behavior.
engineering_relevance: This enables much faster screening of photoactive molecules for optoelectronic device design by replacing many expensive quantum-chemical polarizability calculations with a learned surrogate.
method: Uses an equivariant GNN to respect molecular geometry and tensor symmetries.
Inputs readily available information such as 3D structure and UV-vis spectra.
Predicts complex-valued, frequency-resolved polarizability tensors for downstream optical simulations.
evidence_signal: The model was tested on QM9 and Harvard organic photovoltaic molecules, reproduced main polarizability features, and achieved device-level charge-carrier generation rates that agreed with TD-DFT results with R² = 0.94.
watch_item: Performance may depend on training-set coverage and the quality of available molecular geometries/spectra, so out-of-distribution chemistries or device conditions could reduce reliability.
paper_title: Accelerating dynamic polarizability calculations of organic molecules using equivariant graph neural networks
